title: Find the Minimum Area to Cover All Ones II
summary: Given a 2D binary array, determine the smallest total area of three non-overlapping rectangles that cover all the 1's, allowing the rectangles to touch.
statement: Given a 2D binary array, determine the smallest total area of three non-overlapping rectangles that cover all the 1's, allowing the rectangles to touch.
constraints: grid is a binary rectangular matrix containing at least three ones.
Use exactly three positive-area axis-aligned rectangles with disjoint interiors; each rectangle must contain at least one one.
Cover every one and minimize the sum of rectangle areas; rectangles may touch along boundaries.
hints: Three disjoint axis-aligned rectangles can be separated by two parallel cuts or by one full cut and one perpendicular cut on either side.
Enumerate the six layout families and use a tight one-bounding box inside each of the three regions.
Try all horizontal triples, vertical triples, and four T-shaped orientations; reject empty regions.
Any three pairwise disjoint rectangles admit one of these separating layouts; tightening each within its assigned region never hurts coverage or overlap.
editorial: Any three pairwise disjoint rectangles admit one of these separating layouts; tightening each within its assigned region never hurts coverage or overlap.

tests.explanation: A two-cell vertical rectangle at the left and two horizontal rectangles covering the remaining top and bottom ones total area five.
Three one-cell rectangles cover the diagonal ones with total area three.
